topics.topic: Ownership and scope of the complete ordered startup checks
questions: Who owns the complete A17 rule 2 order and the transition between `configuration`'s checks and the later checks: `configuration`, which says it hides the order of the checks, or `instance_lifecycle`, which says it runs that order?

Does `instance_lifecycle` own the complete A17 startup order, with `configuration` hiding only the order inside its initial group, or does `configuration` own the complete order that its Hides section calls “the order of the checks”?
Does `configuration` hide only the order of its own in-memory and path checks, or the complete A17 startup order that `instance_lifecycle` is also said to run?

quotes:
A17: the start checks of rule 2 that need no file, in its one order, over
the settings `runtime_settings` loads as set — the service tokens of the services
`data_provider`'s rights table lists, all or none, the other items present,
each well formed, each secret at least the 32 bytes `data_provider` holds, no
two secrets equal — with the diagnostic naming the failed item and never its
value; that no default is applied (rule 5); an owner-only start when no token
is given (rule 1); and last the path checks of rule 5 that need no file — the
store and the backup location apart, compared with every link resolved. The
checks after them — the backup probe (`backups`), opening or making the store
(`store`) and the listeners — are run in rule 2's order by
`instance_lifecycle`, which calls this module first.

The start and the running instance: `configuration` first, then the backup
probe and `store`, then the listeners at the release's addresses, serving
nothing until every check passed and having `store` remove a store this start
made new when a listener cannot be opened (A17 rule 2); the
owner-only start, which opens the owner interface alone (A17 rule 1, A18
rule 9); the two surfaces, the owner interface's listener opened first; the 60-second pass
of `owner_sessions` and the minute look of `backups` (A13 rule 2, A18 rule 1);
that a restart ends every owner session (A13 rule 2).
judgement.why: `instance_lifecycle` owns the complete process start sequence, while `configuration` owns and hides the order only within its initial group of checks.

topics.topic: Ownership of secret UTF-8 encoding, byte-length validation, and presented-credential comparison
questions: Does `runtime_settings` own only loading raw environment values, or does it also own the byte encoding and comparison of credentials presented later; if it owns only loading, which authentication module owns that comparison and may know its rule?

Which module owns the UTF-8 byte-length rule, given that this passage places it under `runtime_settings` while the same unit says every length check is `configuration`'s and `runtime_settings` owns environment reading only?
Which module owns UTF-8 encoding and the byte representation used for comparison, given that `runtime_settings` owns only environment reading, must not own length checks, and may know only `models`?

Does `runtime_settings` own or perform either byte-length validation or presented-credential comparison, despite its prohibition on item checks and despite those operations belonging respectively to `configuration` and the authentication module?

judgement.why: P5 judged the same ownership and boundary-representation question for UTF-8 secret conversion, byte-length checking, and constant-time presented-secret comparison, and the relevant passages have not changed.

precedent.topic: Ownership and boundary representation of UTF-8 secret conversion and constant-time comparison
quotes:
`module:random_values`. Compare a presented secret with a held one in time
that does not depend on where they differ (A13 rule 7, A17 rule 6).
The presented value and the held value, as bytes.
precedent.why: State 5 fixes the constant-time comparison boundary as byte inputs supplied by owner_sessions and service_access; configuration separately owns checking the UTF-8 byte length of its loaded text.

topics.topic: Ownership and representation of the runtime settings value and schema
questions: Which module owns the settings value and its concrete absent-versus-present representation?
Which module owns the settings type and its field schema, and may both `runtime_settings` and `configuration` depend on that owner?

judgement.why: P9 judged the same question about ownership and representation of the loaded or validated configuration record, and the relevant passages have not changed.

precedent.topic: Ownership and fields of the loaded or validated configuration record
precedent.why: The exact settings and validated-configuration record schemas, field vocabularies and normalized field types belong to State 6, while State 3 already assigns loading to `runtime_settings` and checking and distribution to `configuration`.

topics.topic: Ownership of filesystem path inspection and symbolic-link resolution
questions: May `configuration` perform filesystem resolution of path components and fail on broken links or loops, or must all filesystem access belong to the later `store`/`backups` checks because these checks are said to need no file?

Are filesystem inspection and symbolic-link resolution part of `configuration`, or are these checks to be performed by `instance_lifecycle`, `store`, or `backups`; what does “need no file” mean when every link must be resolved and unresolved or broken paths fail?

quotes:
A17: the start checks of rule 2 that need no file, in its one order, over
the settings `runtime_settings` loads as set — the service tokens of the services
`data_provider`'s rights table lists, all or none, the other items present,
each well formed, each secret at least the 32 bytes `data_provider` holds, no
two secrets equal — with the diagnostic naming the failed item and never its
value; that no default is applied (rule 5); an owner-only start when no token
is given (rule 1); and last the path checks of rule 5 that need no file — the
store and the backup location apart, compared with every link resolved.
Path resolution and the order of the checks.
judgement.why: `configuration` expressly owns the path-separation check with every link resolved and hides path resolution; “need no file” distinguishes this check from probing the backup location or opening or creating the store.

topics.topic: Orchestration of runtime-settings loading and configuration validation
questions: Does `configuration.load_configuration` call `runtime_settings.load_runtime_settings`, or does `instance_lifecycle` call both and pass the loaded settings into `configuration`?

quotes:
`module:configuration`. Check the settings `runtime_settings` loads in A17
rule 2's order up to the store and backup location apart.
None; it takes the settings from `runtime_settings.load_runtime_settings`.
judgement.why: State 5 specifies that `configuration.load_configuration` itself takes the settings from `runtime_settings.load_runtime_settings`, while `instance_lifecycle` calls `configuration.load_configuration`.

topics.topic: Ownership and lifecycle interface for opening and closing listeners
questions: Which module owns opening and closing the owner-interface and service-API listeners, and what direct dependency does `instance_lifecycle` use to invoke it?

quotes:
The start and the running instance: `configuration` first, then the backup
probe and `store`, then the listeners at the release's addresses, serving
nothing until every check passed and having `store` remove a store this start
made new when a listener cannot be opened (A17 rule 2); the
owner-only start, which opens the owner interface alone (A17 rule 1, A18
rule 9); the two surfaces, the owner interface's listener opened first; the 60-second pass
of `owner_sessions` and the minute look of `backups` (A13 rule 2, A18 rule 1);
that a restart ends every owner session (A13 rule 2).
The process's start sequence, its timers and the two listening surfaces.
judgement.why: `instance_lifecycle` owns the listener portion of startup and the two listening surfaces, and its declared direct dependencies include both `service_api` and `owner_interface`.

topics.topic: Ownership and publication of the environment-variable table
questions: Does `runtime_settings` own the table, or does the module that owns `config.runtime_environment_variables` own and export it; if the latter, what dependency lets `runtime_settings` read it?

quotes:
A17 rule 1's reading of the environment, and only it: the closed table of
the `REGISTRY_` items — the store's location, the backup location, the
backup key, the owner credential, the four service tokens — loaded at each
call of `load_runtime_settings` into the settings. The table holds, for each
item, its variable's name, the settings field it fills and its type, which
is text; nothing else.

The table is its own: the data closure
writes it once, as `config.runtime_environment_variables`, and no other
module holds a name.
judgement.why: The table belongs to `runtime_settings`; `config.runtime_environment_variables` is the generated location where the data closure writes that single table, not a second owning module.

topics.topic: Ownership of rollback and cleanup after a failed startup
questions: Which module owns A17 rule 2's rollback after a later startup failure, including closing an already opened listener and removing a newly made store when possible?

quotes:
The start and the running instance: `configuration` first, then the backup
probe and `store`, then the listeners at the release's addresses, serving
nothing until every check passed and having `store` remove a store this start
made new when a listener cannot be opened (A17 rule 2); the
owner-only start, which opens the owner interface alone (A17 rule 1, A18
rule 9); the two surfaces, the owner interface's listener opened first; the 60-second pass
of `owner_sessions` and the minute look of `backups` (A13 rule 2, A18 rule 1);
that a restart ends every owner session (A13 rule 2).

The one SQLite database (L19) and its connections — the one the
transactions of actions run on, and the read connection a backup's copy
takes its snapshot on while they go on, under the engine setting State 6
fixes, the snapshot fixed by its first read, of the audit counter, with the
clock read then (A18 rule 1): opening it for reading and
writing at start, or making a new, empty store of the release's version —
holding no record but M12 AuditSequence at 0, which the release's statements
make with the store, so `store` needs nothing from `audit_log` — under
the temporary name and renaming it once complete, after removing a leftover of
that name and no other file (A17 rule 5), and removing a store it made new
when the start then fails at a listener (A17 rule 2); the full integrity check —
`PRAGMA integrity_check` answering `ok`, `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` finding
nothing — and the store version check (A17 rule 5), the same check `backups`
asks of a backup's copy.
judgement.why: `instance_lifecycle` owns startup rollback orchestration and directs `store`, which owns removal of a store it made new, when listener startup fails.
